references.text: The basis for the death penalty for murder was established in Noah's covenant: 'Whoever sheds human blood, by humans shall their blood be shed, for in God's image he made mankind.'
Reiterates the principle of the death penalty for killing: 'Whoever strikes a person down shall die.'
Confirms the law: 'Whoever strikes a person down shall die.'
Elaborates on the laws concerning killing and specifies various ways in which one person may kill another, with the death penalty as the consequence.
Gives further instructions that the murderer must die, and that no ransom is to be accepted for the life of a murderer.
Describes the procedure for handling someone who intentionally kills their neighbor, stating that they are to be handed over to the avenger of blood to die.
Jesus refers to this principle when he says: 'For all who take up the sword shall perish by the sword.'
Numbers 35:16 specifies the criteria for a killing to be classified as murder punishable by death.
Leviticus 24:18 creates a theological contrast that highlights the unique value of human life in Exodus 21:12.
Exodus 21:20 elaborates on the principle of retribution for killing by including cases where the victim is a slave.
Numbers 35:18 expands the definition of murder to also include the use of dangerous instruments.
Numbers 35:17 confirms that using a hand-held stone also qualifies the act as murder.
Numbers 35:20 defines the subjective motive (hatred and premeditation) required to incur the death penalty.
